text.p: Most base metal prices sagged during the latter part of a dull Monday LME session, pulled down by copper, although aluminium was an exception, traders said.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index added 0.06 points to 243.75.

The aluminium market shrugged off a rise in June IPAI producer inventories, and rallied away from near $1,730 support on fund buying. By the close prices were at $1,750, up $4, with last week's $1,775 highs back in sight, some said.
Copper fell prey to stale bull liquidation this afternoon, with some sell-stops triggered, and the market briefly tested $2,270 before ending at $2,274, down $14.
Zinc wobbled as well during the kerb, but still finished just $2 lower at $1,545. September tightness continues to cushion the market, with cash/threes at $155/175 backwardation.
Nickel extended earlier declines during the afternoon, with the retreat accelerating on the kerb as the market fell through $6,900.

Lead lurched lower this afternoon as well, briefly threatening to fall under $600 and set a new 22-month low before modest support near "the figure" emerged. Nevertheless, last trade was at $605, down $9.
Tin matched the trend, and closed $85 lower at $5,520, while alloy ended at a steady $1,540/45 a tonne.

COMEX gold and silver futures ended higher Monday, helped by ongoing nervousness about the direction of U.S. stocks and bonds. COMEX December gold ended up $2.10 an ounce at $332.50, , its highest level since late July, but total COMEX gold volume was light at around 29,000 lots. December gold has been in a $320-335 range since early July. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $328.20/70 an ounce, compared to the London Monday afternoon fix at $327.70 and the New York close Friday around $326.90/40.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on a drop in corn and soybean futures, traders said. Corn and especially soy were pressured by showers over the weekend in portions of the U.S. Midwest and on forecasts for more rain early this week in the key dry areas of the corn and soybean growing region. Wheat closed 1-1/4 to five cents lower, with September down 3-1/2 at $3.63-3/4 per bushel.

IPE Brent crude oil saw a slight recovery just before the close on Monday after a fairly uninspiring days trade, brokers said. September Brent on the IPE closed up 10 cents at $18.58 a barrel in what brokers saw as a consolidation following the losses seen at the end of last week. On Friday the prompt Brent contract slid 42 cents. "We've just been consolidating today. It's been very boring and we saw a moderate recovery at the end from some MOC (market on close) buying," one said.
